name: Staircase
description: Endless staircase pad: stacked octaves that glide, step by semitones or walk up the held chord forever without arriving.

params.name: Motion
params.description: How the sound climbs: a glide without end that leaves the key, steps of a semitone, or a walk through the notes of the held chord. One key alone walks by octaves.

params.name: Speed
params.description: How fast the sound climbs, or falls when it is negative. At zero nothing moves and it is a plain pad on the note.

params.name: Centre
params.description: Where the sound is strongest for middle C. Lower is darker and heavier, higher is thinner and brighter. A key an octave higher sits half an octave higher.

params.name: Span
params.description: How many octaves sound at once. Narrow is one clear register, wide a full organ from deep to high. In Chord a key sounds every third octave and Span is four or more.

params.name: Shape
params.description: From pure tones to a brighter, reedier wave: adds the odd overtones of every octave without changing the loudness.

params.name: Slide
params.description: How smoothly a step moves to the next: from a jump at once to a glide that lasts the whole step. It does nothing while Motion is Glide.

params.name: Chorus
params.description: Adds a second, quieter set of the same octaves a few cents apart, drifting slowly against the first. At zero there is one set.

params.name: Attack
params.description: How long a note takes to fade in. Short speaks at once, like an organ; long is a slow swell.

params.name: Release
params.description: How long a note takes to fade out after the key is released. A fading note keeps climbing with the rest.

params.name: Width
params.description: How far the sound spreads to left and right. Neighbouring octaves sit on opposite sides and sway as they climb; in Chord each key takes a side. At zero it is mono.

params.name: Volume
params.description: Output level of the instrument. A soft clip after it rounds off the peaks when many notes stack up.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit. It models the octave-stack illusion of a tone that rises without end: sines an octave apart under a raised-cosine bell over log frequency that follows the played key by half, with a chord walk added. The bell, the odd-overtone shape and the delay chorus are simplifications, and it is not a model of any one instrument or product.
